a.text: So this is what heaven looks like to those insigniﬁcant souls.
For the first time, I walked out of the chaos and void into these vast lands.
Where did I come from, and where am I going?
I still carry memories of that enormous body, and I seem to have some kind of divine power as well as a lifespan that far exceeds those of the masses I see before me.
But like a confused child, I followed the people I saw and imitated what they did.
After a great length of time, I met two teachers.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: There is a barren swath of land in the northern reaches of Yan.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: I'm trying to reclaim and farm the uncultivated fields there with the locals. It's fun to watch crop after crop grow out of the soil. If you don't know where to go, why don't you come give us a hand?

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: Hm... It's much colder than the towns here. Plus, those things from beyond the door are a bit dangerous.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: But you wanted to find out what 'man' is like. It might just be the perfect place for you.

steps.name: Shu
steps.text: You'll have all the time you need to find your answer.

a.text: That was when I found out for the first time that there was such a concept as 'comradery' between living beings.
Maybe this is why they were able to defeat those enormous beings?

steps.name: Hardworking Farmer
steps.text: How strange. It was hailing furiously last night, but the crops are all fine.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Maybe luck is on our side? Maybe Heaven saw how hard we worked the fields and decided to have mercy?

steps.name: Hardworking Farmer
steps.text: Ji, this is your doing, isn't it?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: I simply thought it would be a shame for a hail to destroy the hard work and effort that everyone put in over the last six months...

steps.name: Hardworking Farmer
steps.text: Everything in this world lands moves according to its own set of rules. When a season's harvest is ruined, you can bury it to fertilize the soil and help the next year's crops grow even better.

steps.name: Hardworking Farmer
steps.text: You saved this field's harvest this season, but how many fields are there like this one in Yan? How many mouths are there to feed at the mercy of Heaven?

steps.name: Hardworking Farmer
steps.text: You did this out of the kindness of your heart, but mankind needs to learn to survive on these lands by itself.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Will you leave one day, too?

steps.name: Hardworking Farmer
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Hardworking Farmer
steps.text: But this swath of land will be here forever. Life will exist forever.

a.text: Everything under Heaven has its own position.
But we live between Heaven and earth, like rootless trees, destined to drift about.
No cause and no effect. No beginning and no end.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: You're a merchant here for grain, you say?

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: There are droughts everywhere this year. I heard the granaries in the north have a surplus, so I'm here to purchase grain to resell where the situation is more dire.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Heaven and her rainstorms show no mercy. The farmers have it hard.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: A famine year's not necessarily a bad thing for farmers, though.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: You speak nonsense, my good gentleman. How could a famine be a good thing for the farmers?

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: Simple wisdom. The more severe the famine, the more their harvests earn them.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: Compare five hundred catties at one wen per catty to a hundred catties at ten wen per catty. Even a three-year-old can calculate which is the better deal, from a seller's perspective.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: I've lived here ever since I was a child. The only way I know to use food is to feed the masses and save lives.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: To think such wisdom existed in the lands outside.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: You haven't seen what it's like outside Dahuang. Not everyone is a Xian that can see only the abyss but not the water that fills it. If all one does is guard these plots, how is he or she meant to understand all the wisdom under Heaven?

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: Young man, my caravan needs someone to help manage our affairs. Might you be interested in coming with us to the lands outside?

steps.name: Tea Leaf Peddler
steps.text: Get me a room.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: Per the old rules, the cargo goes in the warehouse. You pay first, then you get your room.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: You said you wanted to get in the tea business because of all the tea farms sprouting up around Shangshu over the last two years. How come you bought out these inns instead?

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: How much do you reckon a truckload of 'Shangshu Greens' can earn when transported from here to Baizao, and how much in tariffs will the court take?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: If the journey to Baizao is uneventful, a twenty-percent profit would be a fairly good return to me.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: Now how much do you reckon I can make here with all the tea merchants coming and going, even the ones unwilling to pay their taxes?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: When you put it that way, certainly you are in a more lucrative business.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: But I also noticed that you withheld some of the cargo for the mandarins?

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: Now that is my other line of business.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: The people working in the government need something to show, too.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Are you not afraid of the mandarins looking for trouble or the tea merchants turning against you?

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: That wouldn't be a very good bargain to them.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: Without me, the tea merchants would have to pay their fair share in taxes or take the risk to find another route.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: Without me, the government would have to spend a hefty sum to get their hands on tips about smugglers. Or, say the merchants ended up revolting. How much would it cost to quell this revolt?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: A win for all three parties. Indeed, an unusually lucrative line of business.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: We've been in Shangshu for long enough. I'm starting to grow tired of the cuisine here. Let's hand the business off and head east.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: East? What kind of business awaits us there? Mining? Grain transport?

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: Whatever earns us money, that's what we'll do... This time, I mainly want to go home to have a look around.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: You asked me before if there exists a wisdom that stands true everywhere.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: All under Heaven live for profit, and die for profit.

steps.name: Astute Merchant
steps.text: Be it law and morality, faith and honor, there is nothing under Heaven that cannot be accounted for in a ledger.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Thank you for that.

a.text: That is indeed what I saw.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: My dear sister, I've settled an account.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: All these years, each of us have lived lives across Yan and recorded our own gains and losses on our respective ledgers.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Dage found his own path, but he found himself an outlier in this mortal realm, a place in which he cannot love, hate, or even let go. A loss.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Ling has lived a carefree life. This realm cannot bind her. She finds her own joy. A profit.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: And our younger sisters. Not necessarily incisive, but they have little that troubles them. They are breaking even.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: As for Erge, our second-eldest brother... Well, Jie is dead. No matter how you slice it, a tremendous loss.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Our family has been under the Yanese thumb for over a millennium. I truly cannot see how we are gaining anything from this transaction.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Most important... is you, my dear sister.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Has the question of profit really never crossed your mind?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: A substitute?

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: I place my bet on a conclusion. For revenge, and for us.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: How... is it even possible?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: One-twelfth is no match for the whole.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: What are your chances... How confident are you?

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: I've worked this out over a long time...

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: There are nineteen lines on a weiqi board, both horizontal and vertical. All the moves one could make have already been calculated. The white player is compensated seven-and-a-half points, giving black less than half a winning chance.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: Truly, a most difficult task on my own.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: That is why I need your help.

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: If I were to tell you there remains a shred of hope and that this is the one and only way...

steps.name: Wang
steps.text: Would you be willing to put your wealth and life on the line?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: You catch up fast.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Perhaps it's time to give an explanation for your actions.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: What form of explanation would you like, Lord Zuo?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You roused demons to lay harm to the citizenry, seized the country's fortifications, and even plotted against the other proxies.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Given your actions, your crimes are far worse than Wang's.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: I may have some objections to your charges, but what would you like to do here?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Hand over the cloth, and return to the capital under Sui Regulator supervision.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: And what will I get in return?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: A chance at a fair trial.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: A shame that it is not a price I am willing to pay.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You would make an enemy of Yan?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: If I would, what could you possibly do?
Zuo Le takes a step forward and unsheathes his blade.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Is it really so much fun to pick on mortals?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: It's you—?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Not bad, kid. You managed to tail him all the way here. Gotta hand it to you.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: But this is a family matter. You Sui Regulator folks will have to give us some personal space.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: You escaped the heart. You are moving faster than I anticipated. Seems my little sisters have grown up.

spans.text: You are moving faster than I anticipated. Seems my little sisters have grown up.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: Don't talk like we're all getting along.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: What do you think this is, a test? And here I thought you were actually trying to off us.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Don't be ridiculous.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: So you've been laying low all these years to weave this cloth.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Making clothes out of Yan's splendor Not bad.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: He needs this before he goes to see It.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Having travelled all around Yan, I thought it a shame when I finally decided to weave Dahuang into it.

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: So you two are in on this together—

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: And he's finished preparing already...?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: I should've figured. You get along with the weiqi failure the best.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Don't act like you don't know what taking your cloth out of this place means.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: This is a straight-up declaration of war against Yan.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: And?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: You're Sange, my third brother. And truth be told, out of all my older siblings, you're one of the ones I like best. I always feel like the two of us crank out some pretty sick ideas.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Remember how I helped you sell fakes of Dusk's paintings that one time?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: You what?!

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: But I'm sorry, this is way overdoing it, even for me.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: A shame.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: From the looks of it, you're not on my side either, Dusk?

steps.name: Dusk
steps.text: In your dreams.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: It's been a few centuries since we've had a family reunion with more than three of us. To think that the first thing we'd be doing is fighting among ourselves, just like all those years ago.

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: What's the deal? Reminiscing on old times?

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: If we can talk this out peacefully, I would rather us not come to blows.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: How could I possibly raise a hand against my little sisters?

steps.name: Nian
steps.text: Drop the big talk already. It's two against one. The odds are stacked against you.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: Well, we'll just have to see how it all turns out, then.

steps.name: Ji
steps.text: This time, not even the army of that great wild hunt years ago could stop me.
